content_of_post_to_answer: Why is our mind easily depressed?
answer: The mind is not easily depressed because it is weak; it is because the same system designed to protect us is also designed to constantly scan for threats. We notice losses, failures, and rejection more intensely than ordinary moments of safety because survival depended on remembering danger. The problem begins when the mind treats emotional pain as a permanent reality instead of a passing signal. A depressed state can feel like a truthful description of life, when often it is only a temporary filter through which life is being viewed.
